title: 1986 AHSME Problem 7
statement: The sum of the greatest integer less than or equal to \(x\) and the least integer greater than or equal to \(x\) is \(5.\) The solution set for \(x\) is

solutions.text:
If \(x\) is an integer, then \(\lfloor x\rfloor+\lceil x\rceil=2x,\) which cannot equal \(5.\) If \(x\) is not an integer, then \[ \lfloor x\rfloor+\lceil x\rceil=2\lfloor x\rfloor+1. \] This equals \(5\) exactly when \(\lfloor x\rfloor=2,\) so \(2\lt x\lt3.\)

Thus the correct answer is E.
hints: Treat integer and noninteger values of \(x\) separately
For noninteger \(x,\) the ceiling is one more than the floor
